subject.title: perf(usage): incremental per-session usage rollups in per-agent SQLite

question: Is the current benchmark and focused coverage sufficient to accept retiring the legacy aggregate cache, or should the PR first demonstrate a real upgrade from an existing legacy cache row?
rationale: The cache is rebuildable and the implementation appears correct, but changing a persisted checkpoint contract and deleting the old runtime path requires explicit maintainer acceptance of the first-run upgrade behavior.

options.title: Require upgrade proof
options.body: Rebase the branch and demonstrate that an existing legacy cache is discarded, rebuilt once, and produces the same usage response without harming the session database.

options.title: Accept the cold rebuild
options.body: Land after required checks complete, treating the linked benchmark and regression suite as sufficient evidence for the intentional one-time cache rebuild.

recommendation.title: Require upgrade proof
recommendation.body: Rebase the branch and demonstrate that an existing legacy cache is discarded, rebuilt once, and produces the same usage response without harming the session database.

likelyOwner.reason: Has the strongest combined history across the original usage cache, subsequent hardening, and the proposed replacement architecture.
